title: App servers
description: Servers that run the apps your employees build. Workforce OS logs in over SSH with this workspace's own key and never needs the root password.
empty: No server yet. Add one so your employees can publish previews of the apps they build.
emptyReadOnly: No server yet. An Owner can add one here.
ownerOnly: Only an Owner can add, verify, edit or remove servers.
privateAllowed: This installation may also use servers on private addresses (such as 127.0.0.1).

fields.name: Name
fields.hostHelp: Its hostname or public IP address, the one you use to log in with SSH.
fields.usernameHelp: The user the setup script creates for the apps. Keep wfos-apps unless you have a reason to change it.
fields.baseDomainHelp: Each app gets its own address under this domain (app-name.preview.example.com). Point a wildcard DNS record (*.preview.example.com) at this server.
fields.maxRunningAppsHelp: At most this many apps run on this server at the same time. Keep it low on a small server.

addDescription: Register the server first. Next you prepare it with one command and confirm its identity.
resetWarning: Changing the address, port, user or domain resets verification: you will compare the fingerprint again.
deleteConfirm: Remove {name} from Workforce OS? Nothing on the server itself is changed.

setup.title: Set up {name}
setup.description: Four steps. You need a terminal on that server, logged in as root or as a user who can use sudo.
setup.ownerOnlySteps: Steps 2 to 4 (checking and confirming the server's identity) are for an Owner.

step1.title: Prepare the server
step1.intro: Run the setup script once, as root, on the server you are adding.
step1.itemUser: a user named {user} without general sudo rights, which accepts this workspace's key
step1.itemWeb: nginx and certbot, to give every app an HTTPS address
step1.itemNode: Node.js and pnpm, to build and run the apps
step1.itemPostgres: a separate PostgreSQL just for the apps (port 5433), apart from any database already on the server
step1.itemHelper: a small root helper (wfos-app-helper): the only command {user} may run with sudo, and it accepts only a fixed list of checked actions
step1.noPassword: Workforce OS never sees or stores the root password. It logs in as {user} with its own key; anything that needs root goes through the helper.
step1.requirements: Ubuntu or Debian only. It takes about 5 to 10 minutes and is safe to run again.
step1.optionAHelp: Paste it into the server's terminal. It saves both files in a folder named wfos-setup and runs the setup.
step1.optionBHelp: Put prepare.sh and wfos-app-helper in the same folder on the server, then run this command in that folder:
step1.publicKeyHelp: Safe to share: it only lets Workforce OS log in as {user}. It is already part of the commands above.
step1.done: At the end it prints WFOS_SERVER_READY and the server's fingerprint. Keep that window open for the next step.
step1.scriptsMissing: The setup scripts are missing from this installation. Ask whoever runs Workforce OS to update it.

step2.title: Compare the fingerprint
step2.intro: The fingerprint is the server's ID card. Comparing it makes sure Workforce OS talks to your server and not to an impostor.
step2.compare: Run this on the server. The SHA256:… part it prints must be exactly the same, character for character:
step2.match: The fingerprints are exactly the same
step2.mismatch: Different? Stop here. Check the address, and ask your hosting provider whether the server was reinstalled.

step3.title: Confirm and verify
step3.intro: Workforce OS remembers this fingerprint and refuses the server if it ever changes. You will be asked for your password and authenticator code.
step3.needsMatch: Scan the server and tick the box in step 2 first.

step4.title: Result
step4.ready: {name} is verified and ready for app previews.
step4.error: The fingerprint is saved, but the check found a problem:
step4.retry: Fix it on the server, then press Check now.

error.host_key_mismatch: The server's identity (host key) changed after it was verified. If the server was reinstalled, edit it and verify it again; otherwise someone may be intercepting the connection.
error.ssh_auth_failed: The server did not accept this workspace's key. Run the setup script again (step 1) and check the login user.
error.ssh_unreachable: The server could not be reached. Check the address and the SSH port, and that its firewall allows SSH.
error.server_host_not_allowed: This address is private. This installation only connects to servers on public addresses.
error.helper_missing: The helper is not installed on the server. Run the setup script (step 1).
error.helper_outdated: The helper on the server is too old. Run the latest setup script again (step 1).
error.server_domain_mismatch: The server was prepared for a different domain. Run the setup script again with --domain {domain}, or change the server's domain here.
error.unknown: The check failed for an unexpected reason. Try again in a moment.
